newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices seen staying firm.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices seen staying firm.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to remain firm at auctions in Newcastle, Melbourne and Fremantle this week when about 93,600 bales will be offered, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said in its weekly market preview.
Last week's firm tone was expected to remain, particularly for the finer end of the market, with the last of the superfine sales for the season, it said.
This would be the last opportunity for buyers to complete orders for stylish wools, it said.
Reduced quantities overall were expected to put buyers under pressure and maintain the upward price momentum, it said.
Rostered sales for February so far had been revised down by an average of 7,500 bales and for the next three weeks were down by as much as 11,500 bales, it said.
In addition, Wool International stockpile sales were now confined to the June quarter, with those for March now complete.
The last two to three weeks of very wet conditions in Australia's north were also expected to result in rain-delayed shearing, further restricting availability, it said.
Last week the eastern market indicator rose by 13 cents a kg clean to 621 cents a kg, reaching its seasonal peak.
